text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Sunday as reported by the official Algerian news agency APS. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Presidency resumes contacts with opposition. President Zeroual for past few days has been receiving party members with aim of getting them to join National Transitional Council, (Algeria's unelected quasi-parliament).

- President Zeroual receives Said Saadi, head of Rally for Culture and Democracy (RCD) party, to discuss enlarging Transitional Council. Aim is to add parties not yet represented so they can take part in debate on laws governing elections and political parties. RCD rejected offer.
- Presidency holds meetings with political parties to try to get them into Transitional Council to debate laws that will govern promised elections next year.

- "Party for the Revolutionary Family" to hold inaugural congress, which will be attended by satellite bodies of former ruling National Liberation Front (FLN), with support of main workers' federation, UGTA. Meeting will be held next February.
- Initiatives taken to form party grouping families of Algerian revolution. Newspaper questions whether this could spell end of former ruling FLN.
- New rules in draft law on political parties mean "political groups will be called to adapt themselves to real democratic practice".
